authority: WO-172-D012 (operator scope expansion, 2026-09-29), bound by the execution amendment of 2026-09-29T01:17:22.197Z

method.sources: This machine's Claude Code transcripts for the repository and its worktrees (126 project folders) and Codex CLI and VS Code sessions working in it (344 of 725; the 381 subagent threads excluded), read 2026-09-29. The second repair read the same folders and sessions again on 2026-09-29 for VER-002 F4 and F5, and once more after its review; a session that began after activation is outside the subject. A prompt the host marks as sent through its SDK entry point was launched by a tool call and is not read, and a line that the file of a continued session repeats under the same line identifier is read once, in the file that holds the most lines.
method.routes: Claude: a typed turn prompt; a message queued while the agent worked and absorbed into the turn (sent time from its enqueue); a queued message delivered as the next turn (counted once, at its enqueue); an interrupt; an answer to the agent's question tool (each answered result, sent at the result's time, read as its picked labels, its typed values and its typed notes). A message whose body is parts, text beside an image, is read for its text under the route that carried it. Codex: a turn prompt; a prompt while the agent worked; an interrupt; a question-tool answer. Excluded as not the operator's typing: peer-session messages, task notifications, compaction summaries, a scheduled prompt's firings, and injected context, which includes any item a hook injected, whatever the hook is named (WO-172-D015 records a first count that did not separate them). Excluded as the operator's commands to the host or the shell and not messages to a role, with their counts before activation: 365 slash-command invocations (358 the host recorded as user lines and 7 as system lines, under 13 names), 4 of them with arguments of 117 characters in all and 2 queued while the agent worked, and 39 shell commands typed at the prompt, 10 of them queued while the agent worked. A refused question-tool call holds no answer (1). A bare refusal of a tool call carries no typed text (7, none with typed text), and each coincides with an interrupt the survey counts.
method.timing: Sort each session’s operator sends and individual assistant text/tool events by timestamp and source order. A queued message uses its enqueue position. Gaps use the previous operator send and latest dispatch at or before the send (zero on a dispatch itself); context is strictly before that position. Split episodes at an order or role change as well as a gap over 120 s. A question-tool answer is sent at its result's time and the call it answers stands in the context before it.
method.context: The repaired scratch rows retain the full preceding text and last four tool summaries, with their event times. Fields flagged by the clean-room screen are withheld. The historical instigator breakdown is withdrawn as a finding under D018 and is not recomputed from repaired context.
method.classes: The hand classification's eight classes widened with question, ideation, acknowledgement and interrupt; a failure instruction when the message tells a role to record something as a failure; severity when it marks the agent's conduct as seriously short or urgent.
method.readingRules: At the operator's direction (2026-09-29): capitals, profanity and repetition convey how seriously and urgently the agent should have been working, never the operator's state, so no field labels a feeling; the one exception the operator gave is keyboard mash, which the operator reads as extreme, exasperated frustration (three messages, confirmed by the executor from a dictionary screen).
method.classification: The original six-agent classification of 1,703 messages is retained except for three executor-read changes after chronology repair: one answer becomes correction and two become direction. The executor reviewed the available message text and preceding-text excerpts for 408 affected rows and full contexts for the answer cases; 41 rows have a screened field and their historical labels are retained with that limit. No fresh blinded accuracy claim is made. The second repair adds 44 messages. Two classifiers, independent of each other, labelled the 43 question-tool answers and the one message with an image under the same rubric and agreed on every field of every message; the executor read the six typed answers and the five that tell a role to record a failure and kept the labels. A picked option is an answer by rule, and 37 answers hold picks only. One answer's text is withheld by the clean-room screen; it holds picks only, so its class stands by rule and its flags are unjudged. These labels are the classifiers' and the executor's reading, not the operator's.
method.comparison: Jointly by order, recording role and class, match the same UTC day first, then either adjacent day, using each record once within that comparison. Failure instructions are compared with same-role corrections and failed judgments; separate family counts overlap and must not be added. Failed-judgment role means the judge who recorded it, not the executor whose work it judged. Unknown roles and dates do not borrow a known role or date. All episode classes and recorded dispatch classes are counted; only the six shared operator-step classes are matched. Main-checkout episodes remain in the global planning/ideation summaries, without inventing an order. A record entry's role is the recording phase its decision's dispatch identifies, corroborated where needed by that frozen decision or a contemporaneous report explicitly assigning it; a historical, future or support reference alone assigns no role. Uncorroborated roles remain unnamed. A failed judgment's role is its judge's. An order is listed as differing when, in any of its roles, a counted class holds a transcript episode or a record entry without its match, or a failure instruction has no matching record entry. A correction or failed judgment that answers no instruction does not list an order, because the comparison's subject is the operator's instructions: 8 orders hold such entries and are not listed (WO-064, WO-069, WO-090, WO-114, WO-148, WO-151, WO-153, WO-171).
method.limits: Transcripts this machine retains only; 120 of 121 closed orders have sessions here (WO-127 ran from the main checkout, so its record entries have no order-attributed episode). A decision carries a date and no time, and one decision can record several episodes or one episode several decisions, so matching is at day grain. Classes are agent-read with a measured second-pass agreement, not the executor's reading of every message. The first repair kept the identical 2,396 message keys and the retained record-side snapshot; the second removes six keys (one item a hook injected, one prompt launched through the SDK entry point and four lines repeated in a continued session's file) and adds 44 messages under identifiers of their own kind, so every retained key and label still names its message, and it compares against the same record-side snapshot. A day/role match is evidence of co-occurrence, not proof that a particular decision answered that message. Of the original operator-validation sample, four contexts changed; no sampled class was edited. Historical validation remains a measurement of its original presentation, not corrected context. Screened fields and the limited context outside each session constrain classification. A Codex prompt sent while the agent worked carries the time its rollout recorded, because the keypress time is not retained (611 messages). 2 absorbed Claude messages have no enqueue with their text, so their true send time is unknown and their delivery time stands in. Of the frozen record's entries 26 classified dispatches and 3 corrections remain unnamed and cannot match a known role; 27 order-and-role rows are unnamed or undispatched. The third repair corrects 28 role fields from frozen public sources without adding decisions. Of 508 messages queued before activation, 481 were delivered with their text and 1 as parts; 10 were the operator's shell commands, 2 slash commands and 3 a scheduled prompt's firings; the operator withdrew 10; and for 1 the transcript shows no delivery, so it is not counted.

bursts.rule: three or more messages within 30 s
